title: Ultrasound Sonochemistry by Weakening or Breaking Chemical Bonds
role: Research Assistant · Supervisor: Dr. Zihan Wang
description: I worked on piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) for ultrasound-driven chemical processes. My work combined device fabrication with Python-based beamforming on a TI TX7516 platform to concentrate acoustic pressure and investigate cavitation.
detail: The project explored non-thermal release mechanisms and evaluated sonochemical activity using terephthalic-acid fluorescence measurements.

title: Metal Fatigue Crack and Corrosion NDE Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
institution: State Key Laboratory of Millimeter Waves
role: Research Project · Advisor: Prof. Chao Liu
description: I investigated spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) for nondestructive evaluation of metallic surfaces. Using CST and multilayer perceptrons, I studied coupling structures that convert propagating waves into confined surface waves and designed a two-dimensional focusing structure.
detail: The work explored localized field enhancement with a spoof localized surface-plasmon resonator, including crack sensitivity and the influence of sensor lift-off.

title: Multi-source Gesture Recognition Technology for Intelligent Control Applications Based on Machine Learning
role: Team Research Project · Advisor: Prof. Gang Xu
description: Our team investigated radar–vision gesture recognition for intelligent control. The system brings together visual hand features and millimeter-wave radar representations in the time–frequency, range–angle, and range–Doppler domains.
detail: My contributions focused on vision-processing code and hand-motion data collection, including real-time hand detection, tracking, and keypoint-based feature extraction.

title: Near-Field Localization with Programmable Metasurfaces
role: Research Assistant, Summer Research Track · Supervisors: Dr. Kaiming Shen and Prof. Zhiquan Luo
description: I extended the Blind Configuration Method from plane waves to exact spherical waves and developed a joint coherent matched-filter estimator for near-field localization. The work used programmable metasurfaces and received-power measurements to study how wavefront curvature affects position estimates.
detail: I compared plane-wave, Fresnel, and exact spherical-wave models in simulation and on measured datasets, examining phase quantization, sign ambiguity, and the gap between simulation and experiment.

title: Near-Field Focusing via Multi-Dimensional Control Based on AI-Assisted Fast Synthesis
role: Research Proposal · Advisor: Assoc. Prof. Fan Wu
description: This research proposal explores rapid near-field synthesis through joint control of array amplitude, phase, and polarization orientation. The proposed workflow uses full-wave CST simulations to train a forward surrogate, which then guides optimization of focal position, polarization, and sidelobe behavior.
detail: Prepared as an IEEE MTT-S scholarship application project; model training and validation are described as proposed work.
